key_insight: A population balance model can directly track pore size evolution during lyophilization microcollapse and translate it into mass-transfer resistance with predictive accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This offers a computationally light way to forecast product temperature and drying behavior in freeze-drying, reducing reliance on empirical post-hoc resistance fitting.
method: Model pore-size distribution with a population balance equation during primary drying.
Apply the method of moments with interpolative closure to keep computation comparable to standard drying models.
Link pore size evolution to mass-transfer resistance and fit only limited parameters to experimental data.
evidence_signal: The model matched literature cases with both high and low product temperatures, predicted intermediate cases, and agreed quantitatively with multi-experiment data across a range of conditions.
watch_item: The approach depends on calibration of microcollapse kinetics and resistance parameters, so transferability across formulations may require validation.
paper_title: Direct Modeling of Pore Size Evolution and Microcollapse in Lyophilization by Population Balance
